title: Sensor LSTM predicts part dimensions in an injection-molding campaign
summary: A shared bidirectional LSTM with four regression heads predicted weight and dimensions from injection-molding sensor sequences. The campaign collected 132 molding cycles, with 124 retained for regression. On a selected 24-cycle comparison subset, the model reported average MAPE 0.27%. This is an evaluation on the study’s campaign, with epoch selection using held-out folds. Comparators used different evaluation units and protocols, so the reported errors do not establish general model superiority. Generalization across molds, materials, machines and production periods remains untested.
ai_technology: Bidirectional LSTM shared encoder with task-specific MLP regression heads
organization: Clemson University; University of Delaware; University of South Carolina

evidence.tested: Actual molded-part weight, length, width and thickness measurements in a controlled single-factor process campaign. LSTM evaluation used shuffled-cycle five-fold splits and retained each fold’s best epoch on that fold; the cross-method comparison used selected cycles and separate setting-level DOE evaluation.
evidence.unknown: Fold-based epoch selection and selected comparison cycles limit untouched-test interpretation. The protocols/units differ across comparators, so average MAPE 0.27% versus 0.95%/2.03% is not a matched-protocol estimate of universal superiority. No independent production deployment or broader process transfer is established.
evidence.ai_role: The shared LSTM learns temporal sensor features after each complete molding cycle; four MLP heads map them to measured part quality attributes. This is a manufacturing measurement-prediction result, not a newly discovered material property.

source_review.scope: Original complete publisher Methods/Results text independently read, including 132-cycle campaign, 124-cycle regression, selected 24-cycle comparison and fold-based epoch selection. Publication date and affiliations authenticated in original HTML metadata. No raw sensor reanalysis.
